svg.title: ASSURED: from learning to genome-editing evidence
svg.desc: Academy offers 12 lessons. Bench combines design, reagent planning, Sanger trace analysis and clone results. The APOE R176C practice benchmark uses simulated AB1 traces. Actual app-generated guide, edit and silent-blocking annotations are shown. Homozygous example: intended edit 96 percent, accept. Heterozygous example: intended edit 48.2 percent, hold. Partial-conversion example: intended edit 49.7 percent, hold.
svg.text: Learn the principles. Plan your edit. Read the evidence. Choose your next step.

g.text: Orange: silent changes · Purple: intended edit
Select clones · compare edits and support

svg.text: BENCH / DESIGN → ORDER → TRACE ANALYSIS → RESULTS
Annotated chromatogram: guides, cut sites, protein changes and the repaired allele.
Accept · Homozygous for the intended edit

g.title: L173L: clone codon CTC (L), control CTG, designed CTC
Q174Q: clone codon CAA (Q), control CAG, designed CAA
R176C: clone codon TGC (C), control CGC, designed TGC
A178A: clone codon GCT (A), control GCA, designed GCT
V179V: clone codon GTC (V), control GTG, designed GTC

svg.text: Shaded column: designed change (orange blocks a PAM, purple is the edit). Dashed red line: cut.
Red base: differs from the control. Grey block: bases the clone lacks. The clone is laid onto the control at the offset used in the analysis.
Protein row: the control in the reading frame of the design. Box under a clone: its residue at each designed codon (as designed: purple or orange; as the control: grey; other: red).
Design HTML + JSON / AB1 + ZIP import / Clone comparisons / Figure + table exports
